title: What Really Happens on a Gulf Shrimp Boat From Dusk to Dawn — 31 Years, Told Straight
description:
I captained the Lady Beth out of Biloxi for 31 years. Tonight I'm taking you out the way it really goes: from untying at 3:30 in the afternoon to getting paid at sunrise — the try net, the turtle excluder, what comes up in the net that never reaches a grocery store, the storms, and the math on a good night.

On a good night: 1,200 lb of heads-on shrimp at about $3.50/lb at the dock ≈ $4,200. Then fuel (~300 gallons), ice, groceries and repairs, and the crew's shares. What's left pays the boat, the insurance and the captain — on a good night a few hundred dollars; on a bad one, you lose money.

How to help: buy from the boats if you live near the coast; inland, look for "Product of USA · Wild Caught" on the back of the bag.
